title: Unit Economics Dashboard (Console) — UX Spec
author: Alicia Perez
related_pages: ADR-0142: Blended cost per 1M output tokens — canonical definition
SLO: Unit econ metrics data quality SLO
content:
## Overview
This document specifies the Console UX for the internal **Unit Economics Dashboard**, the source of truth for Redwood’s blended inference unit cost reported as **$/1M output tokens** with drilldowns by **model**, **region**, and **customer tier**.

The UX is designed to support three primary workflows:
1) Weekly Finance + Product review of blended unit cost and drivers.
2) Engineering investigation of regressions and optimization levers (cache, quantization, runtime config).
3) Ad-hoc slice-and-dice and exports (tables/CSV) for analysis and executive summaries.

This spec focuses on:
- Information architecture (IA) within Console
- Filter model (dimensions, defaults, persistence, guardrails)
- Drilldown navigation patterns
- Annotated descriptions of key charts and tables
- Data freshness / empty / error states (UX patterns)

Out of scope:
- Canonical metric definitions and reconciliation methodology (see ADR-0142 + data contracts)
- Dataset schema / semantic layer design
- SLOs/alerting implementation details (see SLO doc)

---

## Users and access
### Primary users
- **Finance / FP&A:** Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra and analysts (weekly reporting, tie-outs)
- **Product:** Marissa Cole (Console), Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Aditya Rao (Optimize)
- **Engineering:** Telemetry/Analytics, Observability Data, SRE (debugging regressions and validating fixes)

### Access control assumptions
The default dashboard is internal and broadly viewable by employees. Some slices may be restricted:
- Discount/credit impacts, pricing-sensitive rollups, and any “account-level” customer slices (if/when added) must follow RBAC requirements.

UX requirements:
- If a user lacks access to a restricted view, show **masked values** (e.g., “Restricted”) and a short explanation.
- The page should remain functional; restricted measures should not break layout or filters.

---

## Information architecture (IA)
### Navigation placement
**Console → Analytics → Unit Economics**

Left nav:
- Analytics
  - Usage
  - Latency
  - Errors
  - **Unit Economics** (new)

Rationale: aligns with observability/operations tooling; avoids mixing with billing UI since this is an internal cost dashboard.

### Page layout structure
Single-page dashboard with internal sub-navigation using anchored sections:
1) KPI Strip (top)
2) Trend
3) Breakdowns
4) Drivers & Explain
5) Details Table

All sections respond to global filters.

---

## Global filter model
### Supported dimensions (MVP)
Global filters appear in a fixed header row under the page title.

1) **Date range**
- Options: Last 7 days, Last 14 days, Last 30 days (default), Custom
- Display timezone: UTC (explicit)

2) **Customer tier**
- Values: self_serve, dedicated, private, enterprise
- Default: All tiers
- Multi-select; chips show selected values

3) **Region**
- Values: cloud regions (e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast). Exact list comes from region mapping table.
- Default: All regions
- Multi-select

4) **Model**
- Values: Redwood model identifiers grouped by family/variant (e.g., llama-3.1-70b, mixtral-8x7b, qwen2.5-72b)
- Default: All models
- Multi-select with typeahead search

### Optional (MVP “advanced” toggle)
Hidden behind an “Advanced filters” disclosure to control cardinality and complexity:
- **Quantization profile** (e.g., fp16, int8-w8a16, int4) — only visible when data is present
- **Runtime config / route** (high-cardinality; must be guarded; see Guardrails)

### Filter behavior
- Filters apply instantly on “Apply” button (not fully live as-you-type) to reduce query churn.
- “Reset” restores defaults.
- Filters persist via URL query parameters for sharing deep links.
- The page remembers last-used filters per user (local storage) unless a URL override is present.

### Guardrails & anti-footguns
To prevent unbounded cardinality and slow queries:
- Multi-select caps:
  - Region: max 6
  - Model: max 8
  - Tier: max 4 (all)
- If a user attempts to exceed caps, show inline guidance: “Select fewer values or use the Details Table export.”
- For high-cardinality dimensions (runtime_config/route), require at least one of: Model OR Region selected.

### Filter summary line
Under filters, show a compact summary:
“Showing **All models** · **All regions** · **All tiers** · **Last 30 days** (UTC)”

---

## KPI definitions shown in UI (display only)
The UI references the canonical metrics by display name and tooltip text. Tooltips must match ADR language; do not invent new definitions in the UI.

KPI strip (top) shows:
- **Blended cost ($/1M output tokens)** — primary KPI
- **Output tokens** — denominator visibility and sanity check
- **Compute cost** (component)
- **Overhead allocation** (component)
- **Cache savings (est.)** — displayed as a reduction; tooltip clarifies it is an estimate

Each KPI includes:
- Current period value (based on date range)
- Delta vs previous period (same duration immediately preceding)
- Small sparkline trend (optional if performant)

Tooltips:
- Include “Last updated” timestamp and data freshness status (see Data freshness).

---

## Drilldown navigation model
### Principle
Users should be able to move from high-level blended unit cost → isolate which dimension changed → see driver attribution → export rows.

### Drilldown affordances
- Clicking a bar/legend item adds a filter (drill-in)
- Clicking a table row opens a details drawer and offers “Pin as filter”
- Breadcrumb shows active drill-in steps (e.g., “All → eu-west → dedicated → llama-3.1-70b”)

### Navigation patterns
1) **In-place drill-in (preferred):** clicking visual elements updates filters and refreshes the same page.
2) **Details drawer:** provides additional context without leaving the page.
3) **Explain panel:** contextual driver decomposition for a chosen comparison (see below).

### URL shareability
Any drill-in must update URL parameters so a copied link reproduces the view.

---

## Key screens and annotated mock descriptions

### Screen A — Dashboard landing state
**Header**
- Title: “Unit Economics”
- Subtitle: “Blended cost per 1M output tokens across inference traffic”
- Badge: Data freshness (green/yellow/red)

**Global Filters** (see Filter model)

**KPI Strip**
- Five KPI cards in one row on desktop; wraps to 2 rows on smaller widths.

**Section 1: Trend**
Chart: Line chart “Blended cost ($/1M output tokens) over time”
- X-axis: day (or week when date range > 60 days; V2)
- Y-axis: $/1M output tokens
- Optional second line: previous period (dashed) toggled by “Compare to previous period” switch

Interactions:
- Hover shows tooltip with: date, blended cost, output tokens, compute cost, overhead, cache savings estimate
- Click a point → opens a small popover with “Set comparison A/B” (feeds Explain panel)

**Section 2: Breakdowns**
A 3-column grid of small multiples:
1) “Blended cost by Model (Top 10)” — horizontal bars
2) “Blended cost by Region” — horizontal bars
3) “Blended cost by Tier” — vertical bars or stacked bars depending on selection

Rules:
- Default sorting: highest blended cost first
- Bars show: value label + contribution (optional) if space allows
- “View all” link for Model breakdown opens Details Table with Model grouping pre-selected

**Section 3: Drivers & Explain**
Two-pane layout:
- Left: “Driver indicators” cards
  - Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) with delta vs previous period
  - Quantization adoption (%) with delta
  - Output token mix (avg output tokens/request) with delta
- Right: “Explain cost delta” panel entry point
  - Default state: CTA “Select a comparison to explain”
  - Once comparison selected: shows driver decomposition (see Screen C)

**Section 4: Details Table**
A table with export actions and stable columns for finance reconciliation.

---

### Screen B — Breakdown drill-in (Model → Region → Tier)
Example flow:
1) User clicks bar “llama-3.1-70b” in “Blended cost by Model”
2) Filter chip is added: Model = llama-3.1-70b
3) All charts update; the “Breakdowns” section now changes emphasis:
- “Blended cost by Region” becomes primary (full width) because the next most common drill is region
- “Blended cost by Tier” remains visible

UI details:
- Breadcrumb under title: “All models → llama-3.1-70b”
- A “Clear last drill-in” action appears next to breadcrumb.

Empty state handling:
- If selection results in too few datapoints, show: “Not enough data for this slice in the selected date range.” Provide quick actions:
  - “Expand to last 90 days” (if allowed)
  - “Clear Region filter” / “Clear Tier filter”

---

### Screen C — Explain cost delta panel (integrated entry point)
Note: Detailed UI is specified in DES-212, but this dashboard must provide the entry point and required context.

Entry triggers:
- Compare toggle (Current vs Previous) OR
- User explicitly selects “Comparison A” and “Comparison B” from the trend chart

Panel contents (right-side drawer or embedded card):
- Header: “Explain delta: Blended cost”
- Summary: “+ $0.83 / 1M output tokens (Period B vs Period A)”
- Driver waterfall (or ranked list) with top contributors:
  - Region mix shift
  - Model mix shift
  - Cache hit-rate change (prefix/KV)
  - Quantization profile adoption
  - Overhead allocation change (if applicable)

UX requirements:
- Every driver line must include:
  - Contribution value
  - Short explanation text
  - “View slice” action that applies the inferred filters

Data caveat banner:
- If the comparison touches incomplete partitions: “Some data is still processing; results may change.” Include a link “See freshness” that scrolls to the freshness panel.

---

### Screen D — Details table + export
The Details Table is the “truth table” for analysts.

Default grouping (landing): Date (day)
Alternative groupings (dropdown):
- Date
- Model
- Region
- Tier
- Model × Region
- Model × Tier
- Region × Tier

Table columns (MVP)
- Date (if grouped by date)
- Model
- Region
- Tier
- Blended cost ($/1M output tokens)
- Output tokens
- Compute cost
- Overhead allocation
- Cache savings (est.)
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) (if available)
- Quantization profile (only if filtered to one model OR advanced enabled; to control width)

Actions:
- Export CSV
- Copy query link (copies the current filtered URL)
- “Open in BI” link (if configured; otherwise hidden)

Sorting and pagination:
- Default sort: blended cost descending (except date grouping which defaults to date ascending)
- Pagination: 50 rows/page
- Show total row count and “Top N” indicator if results are truncated by guardrails.

Row detail drawer:
- Clicking a row opens a drawer showing:
  - Mini time trend for that slice
  - Breakdown of component costs
  - Recent related changes (optional V2): rollouts/incidents links
  - “Pin as filter” action

---

## Data freshness, loading, and error states
### Freshness badge
Show a badge near the title:
- Green: “Up to date” (within freshness SLO)
- Yellow: “Delayed” (within warning threshold)
- Red: “Stale” (beyond SLO)

Hover tooltip includes:
- Latest processed partition timestamp
- Expected schedule
- Link: “Data health details” (scroll to footer panel)

### Loading state
- Skeleton UI for KPI cards and charts
- Preserve layout to avoid jank
- Display subtle text: “Querying aggregated unit economics dataset…”

### Error state
If a query fails:
- Inline error module within the affected section (do not blank entire page if only one panel fails)
- Provide:
  - “Retry”
  - “Copy error ID”
  - Link to runbook (internal)

### No data state
If filters yield zero results:
- Show “No data for this selection”
- Suggest actions:
  - Expand date range
  - Reduce filters
  - Check freshness badge

---

## Content design: naming and tooltips
### Naming conventions
- Use “Blended cost ($/1M output tokens)” consistently.
- Prefer “output tokens” (not “completion tokens”) to match internal metering language.
- Use “tier” for self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise.

### Tooltips (must-haves)
Each chart title includes an info tooltip:
- Metric definition summary (1–2 sentences)
- Link to ADR-0142
- Note on what is excluded/included (short, canonical phrasing)

---

## Accessibility and responsiveness
- Charts must have keyboard focus and accessible tooltip equivalents (tab to data series + summary).
- Color usage: do not rely solely on color to show deltas; include +/- indicators and labels.
- Responsive behavior:
  - KPI strip wraps
  - Breakdown charts stack vertically on narrow widths
  - Details table becomes horizontally scrollable with sticky first column

---

## Performance considerations (UX-driven constraints)
- Default landing view must return in <2s P95 for typical internal usage.
- Avoid rendering >10 series lines in a single chart by default.
- “View all” breakdowns should route users to the table rather than expanding chart to hundreds of bars.

---

## Instrumentation (product analytics)
Track the following events (names illustrative; final schema owned by Console analytics):
- unit_econ_view_loaded (with filters, load_time_ms)
- unit_econ_filter_applied (dimension, count_selected)
- unit_econ_drill_in (from_chart, dimension)
- unit_econ_export_csv (grouping, row_count)
- unit_econ_explain_opened (comparison_type)

---

## Open questions / decisions needed
1) **Default comparison**: Should the dashboard always show delta vs previous period on KPI strip, or only when “Compare” is enabled?
2) **Cache savings display**: Present as negative cost component, or as a separate “savings” KPI to avoid confusion?
3) **Overhead allocation transparency**: Do we expose allocation method tooltip text directly in UI or link-only to ADR?
4) **Quantization profile visibility**: Do we show a simple “Quant adoption %” only in MVP, keeping profile-level slicing behind Advanced?
5) **Restricted views**: Which specific measures will be gated in MVP (if any), and what copy should we use for masked states?

---

## Appendix: component checklist (MVP)
| Component | Must-have | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Global filters (date/model/region/tier) | Yes | URL persistence required |
| KPI strip w/ deltas | Yes | Deltas vs previous period |
| Trend chart | Yes | Daily granularity |
| Breakdown by model/region/tier | Yes | Top 10 model bars |
| Explain entry point | Yes | Full decomposition per DES-212 |
| Details table + CSV export | Yes | Stable columns, pagination |
| Data freshness badge | Yes | Green/yellow/red + tooltip |
| Empty/error/loading states | Yes | Section-level errors |
| Advanced filters (quant profile) | Partial | Hidden unless data + safe |
